HackerAI 

 Your AI-Powered Penetration Testing Assistant 

 

 
 

 

 Getting started

Coding agents should start with AGENTS.md.

 Prerequisites

You'll need the following accounts:

 Required: 

- OpenRouter - AI model provider
- OpenAI - Identifies security requests that should use the Inference.net security model
- E2B - Isolated cloud execution in Agent mode
- Convex - Database and backend
- Amazon S3 - File storage
- WorkOS - Authentication and user management
- Trigger.dev - Required durable runtime for agent tasks

 Optional: 

- Inference.net - Security-tuned model for requests that standard models may refuse
- Perplexity - Web search functionality
- Jina AI - Web URL content retrieval
- Redis - Stream resumption
- Upstash Redis - Rate limiting
- PostHog - Analytics
- Stripe - Payment processing

 Clone the repo

 

 Navigate to the project directory

 

 Install dependencies

 

 pnpm build generates Next.js route types and checks them with TypeScript 7
before compilation. TypeScript 6 remains installed as typescript for ESLint,
 ts-node , Convex tooling, and pnpm typecheck . The native compiler is pinned
separately as typescript-build ; build scripts resolve it explicitly rather
than relying on the shared tsc executable name. Use pnpm typecheck for the
TypeScript 6 check; package aliases can expose the same tsc command. Vercel
Preview retains its existing separate CI typecheck. Running next build directly retains Next's
built-in TypeScript 6 check.

 Run the setup script

 

To use the Inference.net security model for eligible security requests, set
 INFERENCE API KEY in .env.local , Vercel, and Trigger.dev and enable the
 inference cyber v1 PostHog flag. Without both, those requests use the selected
model with HackerAI's usual authorization context. Every model provider must
use zero data retention.

 Start the development server

This runs both Next.js and Convex dev servers:

 

Or run them separately in two terminals:

 

 Run the Trigger.dev worker

Agent mode runs the agent loop on a Trigger.dev task.
To use the agent locally:

1. Create a project at and copy your dev secret
 key ( tr dev … ) into .env.local as TRIGGER SECRET KEY .
2. In the Trigger.dev dashboard → your project → Environment Variables ,
 add the env vars the task needs to run (these live on the worker, not on
 Vercel): NEXT PUBLIC CONVEX URL , CONVEX SERVICE ROLE KEY ,
 OPENROUTER API KEY , OPENAI API KEY , AWS S3 ACCESS KEY ID ,
 AWS S3 SECRET ACCESS KEY , AWS S3 REGION , AWS S3 BUCKET NAME , and
 E2B API KEY . Cloud Agent execution uses E2B.
 Add any optional keys you use
 ( INFERENCE API KEY , PERPLEXITY API KEY , JINA API KEY , etc.).
3. Start the worker in a third terminal:

 

 This starts the default Trigger.dev worker used by local Agent requests.
 To start an explicitly routed Trigger.dev branch instead, set a stable
 branch name with
 TRIGGER DEV BRANCH=my-local-agent pnpm dev:trigger . Only use that override
 when the request path is configured to target the same Trigger.dev branch.

install.html:
Coding agents should start with AGENTS.md.

Prerequisites

You'll need the following accounts:

Required:

  • OpenRouter - AI model provider
  • OpenAI - Identifies security requests that should use the Inference.net security model
  • E2B - Isolated cloud execution in Agent mode
  • Convex - Database and backend
  • Amazon S3 - File storage
  • WorkOS - Authentication and user management
  • Trigger.dev - Required durable runtime for agent tasks

Optional:

  • Inference.net - Security-tuned model for requests that standard models may refuse
  • Perplexity - Web search functionality
  • Jina AI - Web URL content retrieval
  • Redis - Stream resumption
  • Upstash Redis - Rate limiting
  • PostHog - Analytics
  • Stripe - Payment processing
Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/hackerai-tech/hackerai.git
Navigate to the project directory
cd hackerai
Install dependencies
pnpm install

pnpm build generates Next.js route types and checks them with TypeScript 7 before compilation. TypeScript 6 remains installed as typescript for ESLint, ts-node, Convex tooling, and pnpm typecheck. The native compiler is pinned separately as typescript-build; build scripts resolve it explicitly rather than relying on the shared tsc executable name. Use pnpm typecheck for the TypeScript 6 check; package aliases can expose the same tsc command. Vercel Preview retains its existing separate CI typecheck. Running next build directly retains Next's built-in TypeScript 6 check.

Run the setup script
pnpm run setup

To use the Inference.net security model for eligible security requests, set INFERENCE_API_KEY in .env.local, Vercel, and Trigger.dev and enable the inference_cyber_v1 PostHog flag. Without both, those requests use the selected model with HackerAI's usual authorization context. Every model provider must use zero data retention.

Start the development server

This runs both Next.js and Convex dev servers:

pnpm run dev

Or run them separately in two terminals:

pnpm run dev:next
pnpm run dev:convex
Run the Trigger.dev worker

Agent mode runs the agent loop on a Trigger.dev task. To use the agent locally:

  1. Create a project at https://cloud.trigger.dev and copy your dev secret key (tr_dev_…) into .env.local as TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY.

  2. In the Trigger.dev dashboard → your project → Environment Variables, add the env vars the task needs to run (these live on the worker, not on Vercel): NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL, CONVEX_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_S3_REGION, AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME, and E2B_API_KEY. Cloud Agent execution uses E2B. Add any optional keys you use (INFERENCE_API_KEY, PERPLEXITY_API_KEY, JINA_API_KEY, etc.).

  3. Start the worker in a third terminal:

    pnpm dev:trigger

    This starts the default Trigger.dev worker used by local Agent requests. To start an explicitly routed Trigger.dev branch instead, set a stable branch name with TRIGGER_DEV_BRANCH=my-local-agent pnpm dev:trigger. Only use that override when the request path is configured to target the same Trigger.dev branch.
